info.title: gim-server
info.description: Mock delivery and authentication service for MLS (RFC 9420) end-to-end encrypted IM clients. The server stores and fans out opaque MLS messages and encrypted blobs and never sees plaintext or keys. JSON fields are snake_case, timestamps are integer milliseconds since the Unix epoch, binary values are standard base64. Every non-2xx JSON response has the shape `{"error":{"code","message"}}`.

post.summary: Send a message to a group
post.description:
Stores the opaque MLS message, assigns the next `seq`, and emits a `message` event: `welcome` messages to their `recipients`, other kinds to every member device except the sender.

A `commit` must carry the group's current epoch, otherwise 409 `stale_epoch` (with `current_epoch`); an accepted commit advances the group epoch to `epoch + 1`.

Resending the same `client_id` from the same device returns the stored message with 200 and emits nothing. A decoded payload larger than the server limit (default 262144 bytes) fails with 413.

200.description: Idempotent replay: the message stored earlier for this client_id

403.description: Caller is not a member of the group (`not_member`)

409.description: Commit epoch does not match the group epoch (`stale_epoch`)

get.description:
Returns events addressed to the calling device with `cursor` greater than the given one, ascending. With `wait > 0` and no pending events the request is held open up to `wait` seconds until an event arrives.

If events after `cursor` have been pruned the server responds 410 `cursor_expired` with the current head `cursor`; the client must resync its groups (GET /v1/groups, message history) and continue from that cursor.

schema.description: Last cursor the client has processed

parameters.description: Last cursor the client has processed
parameters.name: cursor

410.description: Cursor is older than the retention window (`cursor_expired`)

get.description:
WebSocket upgrade delivering the same events as GET /v1/events in real time. Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` or, where headers cannot be set, `?token=`.

After the upgrade the server first replays every event after `cursor`, then pushes new ones. Server-to-client frames are JSON text frames:

- `{"type":"event","event":Event}` — one per event, ascending `cursor`.
- `{"type":"error","error":{"code":"cursor_expired","message":"..."},"cursor":<head cursor>}` — sent when `cursor` is older than the retention window, followed by close code 4410. Resync, then reconnect with the given cursor.

An invalid or missing token closes the connection with code 4401. Client-to-server frames are ignored.
